reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) strongly supports the mechanism and outcomes of Ag-induced tribolayer formation in a (TiNbZr)Ag alloy, but it provides no data or discussion on CoCrFeNi-based systems. The key premise that this approach will work in CoCrFeNi is therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Ag addition to a multi-principal-element alloy can promote in-situ formation of an amorphous-crystalline nanocomposite tribolayer containing Ag nanocrystals during sliding in air.
Such a tribolayer can reduce the friction coefficient to ~0.09 and lower the wear rate by two orders of magnitude compared to the Ag-free alloy.
The tribolayer formation mechanism involves environmental oxygen and thermodynamic driving forces (enthalpy of mixing) for Ag nanocrystal nucleation within an amorphous oxide matrix.
This reactive wear protection approach is transferable to other alloy systems, specifically to a CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix.
